entry.title: [VahidOnline] The New York Post reported on Thursday, September 3, citing a senior regional…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

The New York Post reported on Thursday, September 3, citing a senior regional official, that Oman has rejected the Islamic Republic's proposal for jointly receiving service fees from commercial ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The official said Muscat did not even agree to voluntarily receiving environmental and security service fees from ships. A US official also told the New York Post that the terms of the proposed agreement between the Islamic Republic and Oman for revenue sharing have not been finalized.

These remarks came after Hossein Mohebbi, a spokesman for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, had earlier announced that Tehran and Muscat had reached an agreement in this regard.

Reuters reported on July 29 that Oman had presented a plan backed by Persian Gulf countries to the Islamic Republic, according to which the management of the Strait of Hormuz would be conducted regionally, and shipping companies could voluntarily pay amounts to cover the costs of navigation, environmental protection, and search and rescue operations. Oman had previously also opposed the mandatory collection of fees from ships transiting this waterway.

@VahidOnLive📡 @VahidOnline

entry.title: [VahidOnline] 📝 What do we know about the attack on the wedding ceremony in Sirik?…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

📝 What do we know about the attack on the wedding ceremony in Sirik?
🔹Coinciding with US airstrikes on Sirik county on the night of September 1, 2025 (10 Shahrivar 1405), an explosion destroyed a house in Bandar Kohestak where a wedding ceremony was being held. According to published reports, so far five people, including a four-year-old child, have been killed and 65 people injured.
🔹Images from the scene, the sound of multiple explosions in the CCTV video, CENTCOM's statement, and the fact that the attack was not denied by its spokesperson strengthen the attribution of that night's attacks to the US.
🔹Meanwhile, on social media, it was claimed that the house explosion was the result of an "unsuccessful IRGC missile launch"; however, no official report or credible evidence has confirmed this claim so far.
🔹Some accounts have shared old or unrelated videos to prove this claim. The only similar report about an unsuccessful IRGC launch that same night pertains to Khomein in Markazi province and has no connection to Sirik in southern Iran.
🔹Despite evidence pointing to a US attack on Sirik, it is still unclear exactly what projectile struck the house where the wedding was held.
🔹Meanwhile, in the CCTV video, the sound of a drone can be heard, and the bride's father also mentions hearing drones in a video interview; evidence that strengthens the possibility of a simultaneous use of missiles and drones in the operation.
🔹Meanwhile, fragments of a SLAM-ER cruise missile have been seen in the area, but the extent of the house's destruction does not seem consistent with the full detonation of this missile's 360-kilogram warhead.
🔹It is possible that the house was targeted with smaller munitions (for example, a Lucas drone with a warhead of about 18 kilograms), and the SLAM-ER fragments may be related to another strike in the same area (a telecommunications tower about 130 meters away).
👈 Read the fact-check
🌐 @Factnameh

The Supreme Court has upheld the sentence of 12 years, six months, and one day in prison, confiscation of all assets, and a two-year ban from running cafés for Sadegh Saedinia, the manager of the 'Saedinia' chain of cafés. Mizan News Agency, the media arm of the judiciary, announced on Thursday, September 3 (12 Shahrivar 1405) that this sentence was issued due to Saedinia's support for the protests of January 2026 (Dey 1404) and the closure of the union units under this brand. According to the judiciary, Sadegh Saedinia was sentenced to 12 years, six months, and one day in discretionary prison and the confiscation of all his movable and immovable property in favor of the government on charges of 'media and propaganda activity against national security in favor of opposition groups.' The court also sentenced him to a two-year ban from café management after his prison term ends. The judiciary has cited posting protest content on Instagram, supporting calls for protests, closing the cafés and stores of the chain, and encouraging employees to participate in protests as instances of his charges. According to the indictment, Sadegh Saedinia was tried on three charges: 'propaganda or media activity against national security,' 'operational action for groups opposed to the Islamic Republic,' and 'propaganda activity against the regime.'@VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline

entry.title: [VahidOnline] US Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Venezuela's interim President Delcy…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodríguez signed an oil agreement in Caracas on Wednesday, under which the United States gains majority control over 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's oil reserves. This amount represents about one-fifth of Venezuela's vast oil reserves. US President Donald Trump has described the deal as "the biggest oil deal in the history of the world." Under the agreement, the US will have preferential access to 17 Venezuelan oil fields—facilities some of which were previously held by Russian and Chinese companies. Meanwhile, Chevron has also announced a separate $7 billion agreement to develop two other oil fields in the Orinoco Belt. Chevron says this investment could more than double its production in Venezuela within five years. The US Energy Secretary has predicted that Venezuela's oil production will exceed two million barrels per day by the end of this decade—about double the production level in January, when US forces overthrew Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez took power. The agreement has also faced criticism, with detractors accusing Rodríguez's government of surrendering Venezuela's sovereignty over its oil resources. The Venezuelan government, in response, says the deal will help the country harness its energy capacity and attract investment. @VahidHeadline 📡 @VahidOnline

entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

The prices of foreign currencies in Iran set a new record on Wednesday morning, September 1, hours after the new round of U.S. attacks, with the euro, the European single currency, crossing the 255,000 toman mark for the first time. Currency rate websites, including "Nosan," reported the U.S. dollar at around 220,000 tomans. The UAE dirham also rose to over 60,000 tomans. The rise in foreign exchange rates in Iran's free market has intensified since the UAE announced cutting financial ties with Iran and the start of the U.S. economic pressure program called "Operation Economic Rejection." In the past two weeks, Iran's national currency has lost more than 10% of its value against major foreign currencies. On Wednesday, the price of the so-called "Emami" gold coin was reported at 224 million tomans, despite a global decline in gold prices. Abdolnaser Hemmati, the governor of the Central Bank, on September 1, rejected claims of a shortage of foreign exchange resources and the possibility of an economic collapse in Iran, saying the central bank is ready to supply up to two billion dollars to control the market.

entry.summary:

◼️Condolence message from Dr. #Reza_Soleyman_Heshmat on the passing of Dr. Mohammad Reza Rikhtehgaran
The late Dr. Mohammad Reza Rikhtehgaran was a highly virtuous person with a remarkable inner calm and tranquility. He learned a great deal from the late Professor Seyyed Ahmad Fardid and Professor Davari Ardakani, especially in the fields of art and poetry. He also spent time in India researching ancient texts and the culture of the subcontinent, and upon his return, he took on the teaching of the course on wisdom in Asia and the East at the University of Tehran. He was deeply committed to contemplative thought and the philosophical and wisdom traditions in the history of Eastern and Western philosophy. If he leaned toward one side in matters of belief and politics, he never abandoned fairness and moderation.
One of my unforgettable memories with him—after which I never had the chance to see him again—was when, at the invitation of Dr. Ayatollahi, it was arranged for me to speak on "Paradoxy" in Hafez, Kierkegaard, and Nietzsche at the House of Humanities Thinkers, and he was to serve as the discussant. It was a good session. Afterward, he called and expressed his kindness and appreciation. What I remember is that I said the core point, of course in Derrida's terms, goes back to Heidegger's two-fold dialectic and the late Fardid's insights on opposites, but the detailed exposition was my own, and naturally any errors or shortcomings in it were mine.
Once again, I ask God Almighty for forgiveness, mercy, and elevation of rank for the deceased, and for patience and reward for his family, friends, and admirers. Undoubtedly, Iran's academic and scholarly community will always benefit from his written works, God willing.
🖋 Reza Soleyman Heshmat
1405/06/11

entry.summary:

The next main risk is not a single retaliatory strike; it is the normalization of periodic attrition operations aimed at preventing Iran's capability rebuilding. The simultaneous message of "response to regional facilitators" and "return to understanding" is likely a combination of deterrence and keeping an exit route open; without a unified stance, it may be interpreted by Gulf states as a direct threat and by the US as a lack of negotiating authority. The fresh attack on the tanker shows that even without a second official US wave, the maritime insecurity cycle continues independently of diplomacy. The zeroing out of observable liquid tankers and the drop in US strategic reserves to about 286.6 million barrels further narrows the market's tolerance margin; however, no new and quantified supply disruption has yet been proven.

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] The erosion of war and the capacity to think... Once again, American military…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

The erosion of war and the capacity to think... Once again, American military drones, missiles, and bombs have rained down on the people of the country's southern cities. Alongside material damage, a number of our compatriots have been killed. A wedding ceremony in Kohestak turned into a mourning gathering. In response, Iranian forces also targeted American bases in the Middle East with missiles. Everyone is asking: how long will these clashes continue, and where will they end? The truth is that there is no clear answer to these two questions. The American side holds contradictory positions. On one hand, they emphasize continuing pressure until the collapse of our country's security and economy, and on the other hand, they claim the goal of the pressure is to force the leaders of the Islamic Republic back to the negotiating table! On the Iranian side, despite the constant insistence by responsible officials on the need for social unity and cohesion, no single voice is heard regarding the war. While the leaders of the branches of government declare their goal to be the revival of the agreement and forcing America to implement its provisions, many other voices from within the establishment insist on opposing the agreement, continuing and expanding the war, and the necessity of resorting to preemptive operations. As such, the atmosphere on both sides of the war is ambiguous and unclear. As long as this remains the case, the war will continue intermittently along its current erosive path. The main issue, however, is: to what point can the war of attrition in its current form continue? It is clear that capacities on both sides of the war are limited, and it is impossible to sustain the current conditions even for the next few months. Therefore, it is highly likely that a dramatic event will change the current course. What will be the nature of that event, and in what direction will it shape the fate of the conflict? The nature of an "event" is its chance and accidental occurrence, and it is not predictable. Any prediction in this regard is like shooting an arrow in the dark. Even if such an arrow hits its target, it is by chance and not a sign of the predictor's knowledge and skill! In our culture, these events are called fate and destiny (qaza va qadar), and now our fate is tied to fate and destiny. All we can do is pray that the outcome is good. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] "This caravan of life passes wondrously." Twenty years ago, after completing my…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

"This caravan of life passes wondrously." Twenty years ago, after completing my philosophical studies at the University of Warwick in England, I returned to Tehran and, as a faculty member and assistant professor, began teaching and researching at the "Iranian Institute of Philosophy." During that five-year period, my office was near Dr. Behzad Salki's office. For this reason, on average, we saw each other twice a week; either he would come to my office, or I would go to his, and we would drink tea and talk together. I remember that in our first meetings, we discussed the book "Philosophy of Religion" by John Hick, which had been translated by him and published under the name Behzad Rad. In the 1990s (1370s), when I was a pharmacy student, a few friends interested in philosophical topics and I would read different chapters of Hick's translated book weekly and discuss them. Later, in the 2000s (1380s), we discussed John Hick's "The Fifth Dimension," which had been translated into Persian by Behzad Salki, with several philosophy-researching friends. At that time, I did not know that the translator of both books was the same person, and that Behzad Rad was the pen name of Mr. Behzad Salki. When I mentioned this to Behzad Salki, he laughed and said: "I preferred that at that time, Hick's works, which had just come before the eyes of Persian-speaking philosophy researchers, not be published under my name, because 'the passage of well-being was narrow.'" Dr. Salki was a pleasant, humble, and sincere person, and a tranquility emanated from him. He had nothing to do with anger, jealousy, or harshness, and he enjoyed great mental health. I do not recall him speaking ill of anyone. In our conversations, we talked about the books we were reading and our work and research projects. He was aware of my great fondness for Sepehri and Wittgenstein, and out of kindness, he introduced me to some good Persian and English works in these areas, most of which I read with enthusiasm. He had a close friendship with the esteemed professor Baha' al-Din Khorramshahi. He had interesting memories about the process of translating the book "A History of God" by Karen Armstrong, which had been translated into Persian by Khorramshahi and him, and I delighted in hearing them....👇👇👇 https://www.instagram.com/p/Dcwpaucx867/?igsi=N3k3MHY5bmliZjRn

The dollar price in Iran's open market reached 213,700 tomans, and the dollar remittance rate hit 218,000 tomans. The British pound was also traded at 289,000 tomans. Unfrozen reserves, sustainable resources, and numerous oil and non-oil revenues are available to the Central Bank.' He added that the Central Bank allocated $500 million to the market last week and is now ready to inject up to $2 billion in currency if needed. Today's remarks by Hemmati differ from his previous stance. Last week, in a television interview, he had said: 'Our income from oil sales has dropped to zero; it's a fact that we are not exporting oil.' The shift in tone came after a message from Mojtaba Khamenei, the leader of the Islamic Republic, on the occasion of Government Week. In that message, he said that sometimes honestly expressing weaknesses helps the enemy and emphasized the need to 'explain and narrate Iran's power and strength.' entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] At 61! Today I turned 61; of course, according to what's written in my ID,…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

At 61! Today I turned 61; of course, according to what's written in my ID, otherwise, according to my sisters, I was born in "Kol Kar," meaning the cotton planting season, which falls in April, from late Farvardin to mid Ordibehesht. Honestly, when I look back, I'm quite astonished at my own situation. The factors that came together to bring me from "Qaleh-ye Zardu," where I fell onto the mud floor of a dark, smoky room, to this vague present point—it's been like walking on quicksand. Was everything that happened mere coincidence? One could call it coincidence, especially in this century where not just an individual's life path but the entire universe is considered random, the result of blind forces colliding! Nevertheless, I believe every person assumes some kind of plan or destiny in the course of their life's evolution. Even those who believe in the randomness of existence are tempted, when facing grave dangers or remarkable successes, to seek an interpretation beyond pure chance in their lives. In any case, I have personally experienced something in my life with all my being: whenever, for whatever reason, my head bows from the sky toward the earth, an unpredictable and entirely unplannable event lifts my head upward. I have such faith in this experience that even if, hypothetically, all sciences and philosophies were to conclude that there's nothing up there, it would have the slightest effect on my faith in this experience! Based on my inner and outer experiences, I have accepted that not only is there something up there, but everything ends and culminates there. Hence, the most delightful and sweetest moments of my life have always been when I hold my head high. It's clear that by "up" I don't mean the geographical sense of the word. Up exists in all dimensions of being and in all directions. This too is a way of living in an era that some have perhaps wrongly or exaggeratedly called the age of the eclipse of God!#Ahmad_Zeydabadi @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Mischievous fabrication! A friend who specializes in identifying the history of…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Mischievous fabrication! A friend who specializes in identifying the history of films informed me that Hassan Rahimpour Azghadi's remarks about the hijab of an "old and ugly" woman had nothing to do with Ms. Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, and that the video circulating on social media linking the two was a media prank! That's why I deleted my previous post. Indeed, media mischief has reached a point where it's become extremely difficult to tell milk from buttermilk. entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] Last week, to find an answer to the question posed by the esteemed website…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Last week, to find an answer to the question posed by the esteemed website "Sedanat" about the names of Iranian and non-Iranian thinkers and intellectuals (including philosophers, psychologists, poets, novelists, etc.) who, over the past few decades, have played a role in shaping and consolidating my intellectual and written work, and from whom I have received tangible and palpable influences, I retreated to a corner. I rode on the wings of memories and, to the best of my ability, delved into the labyrinthine fortress of memory, the readings, writings, and lived experiences of the past thirty-five years. It was a nostalgic and soul-nourishing journey. The outcome of this inner journey, which started on its own and arrived at its own conclusion, was as follows: names with whose works, teachings, intellectual sparks, and existential embers I have been intimately familiar and conversant for many years, breathing in their atmosphere. A long-standing companionship and association that has also spilled into my essays, books, and lectures: Abu al-Hasan Kharaqani, Abu Sa'id Abi al-Khayr, Sheikh Shahab al-Din Suhrawardi, Saadi, Rumi, Shams Tabrizi, Hafez of Shiraz, Kant, Kierkegaard, Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Jung, Kazantzakis, David Ross, Wittgenstein, Heidegger, Forough Farrokhzad, Abraham Maslow, Albert Camus, Erich Fromm, Ali Shariati, Sohrab Sepehri, Akhavan Sales, Abdolhossein Zarrinkoub, Shamlou, Isaiah Berlin, Gadamer, John Hick, Simin Daneshvar, Dariush Shayegan, Dariush Ashouri, Abdolkarim Soroush, Mojtahed Shabestari, Mostafa Malekian, and Irvin Yalom. https://www.instagram.com/p/DcrMtPfqnIv/?igsi=MzZhZTJiZW9kaXZj

"Forgotten" for Journalists
The documentary "Forgotten," directed by Mehdi Afsharnik, will be screened on Wednesday, September 11, at the Department of Environment, with the presence of department officials, journalists, environmental experts, and activists. This screening, coinciding with the escalating debates over the development of the Sohrab oil field and the relationship between the oil industry and Hor al-Azim, could pave the way for a serious dialogue among officials, critics, and the filmmakers.
The Wednesday screening at the Department of Environment gains even more significance because department officials, experts, and environmental journalists are set to watch together a film that narrates part of the very controversy that has returned to the forefront of discussions today with the Sohrab field case. A film that, on one hand, critiques oil and, on the other, does not align with part of the prevailing environmental narrative; a combination that will likely make the post-screening session as compelling as the film itself.

The Washington Post, citing informed sources, reported that several senior U.S. military officials have warned Pete Hegseth, the U.S. Secretary of Defense, that continuing large-scale military operations against the Islamic Republic is unsustainable and would weaken the U.S. military's ability to counter other threats, including defending U.S. territory. According to these individuals, these warnings—which the chiefs of the Army, Navy, and Air Force, along with the four-star commanders responsible for U.S. military operations in Europe, Asia, and Latin America, presented to Hegseth in the August 14 version of the "Secretary of Defense's Orders Book"—are part of a classified document. According to the report, given Trump's emphasis that the military option remains on the table, the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM), which is responsible for managing the war with the Islamic Republic, has kept more than 50,000 troops on standby for months to act if the President orders further strikes. According to informed sources, the August 14 version of the Secretary of Defense's Orders Book stipulated that some forces deployed in the Middle East would remain in the region until the end of September, and the missions of others would be extended until 2027. The possibility of further extensions of these deployments prompted military commanders to openly raise their concerns. According to these sources, senior commanders of European Command, Pacific Command, and U.S. Southern Command, along with the senior Navy commander, have recorded a "non-concurrence" opinion in this document; meaning they do not agree with the Secretary of Defense's order to extend their forces' deployments, but they will execute it. @VahidOOnLine📡 @VahidOnline

"Happy were the times spent with a friend." These days I am traveling in Europe. Yesterday, I found the opportunity to sit with Mohammad Rahbar at one of the Iranian coffee shops in London, where the scent of Hafez and the city of Shiraz wafts through the air, and we talked for a few hours. It was a valuable meeting; about politics, literature, poetry, reading, and writing... we spoke and listened. Dear Mohammad, in the early days of the forty-day war, he showed admirable courage and integrity by leaving the "Iran International" media outlet; a media outlet that, at least during the twelve-day war and the forty-day war, sadly mixed oil and water, engaged in lies and fabrication, and played a significant role in constructing and reinforcing a narrative that sought to normalize war, as I mentioned in the essay "War, Narrative-Building, and Political Blockage," leaving behind a bitter and shocking anti-patriotic record. Moreover, some Persian-speaking employees of this outlet, during the days when the slingshot of fate rained stones of sedition and missiles rained from the sky onto their compatriots inside the country, leaving them wounded and dead, sat opposite a prime minister who has been called a war criminal by international courts, and with smiles on their lips and body language that reeked of satisfaction and joy, interviewed the main person responsible for the aggression against their country's land and waters, and their disgrace fell from the rooftop for all to see. If I were in the place of those who set about justifying the crime at the Minab school and whitewashing the blatant aggression of Israel and America against their country's soil over the past year, who broke all the pots over the Islamic Republic's head and did not say a harsher word to the enemy of their land and water than a delicate flower, I would melt with embarrassment and feel ashamed. Not to mention that some of these same media figures, using the pure blood of dear young people who were sadly and unjustly spilled on the ground in January of last year as a pretext, made mountains out of molehills without any basis or sufficient evidence, and in their videos fed blatant lies to the helpless, desperate, and oppressed people, earning more audience and making money for themselves: it is fitting that blood surges in the heart of the ruby-colored mourning, for shards are breaking the market of the potter. I am glad that dear Mohammad, despite all the insults and accusations he heard, despite all the arrows of blame fired at him by former colleagues, was not intimidated by the atmosphere; he held his head high, steeled his resolve, and left this organization and media outlet, which, whatever it is, is not national-patriotic, and came to a good end: Two things are the fruit of life: a good name and reward; if you pass beyond these two, all that is on it shall perish. https://www.instagram.com/p/DcoIobjMo54/?igsi=dnp6MzVzajY0djFj

entry.title: [VahidOnline] Duolingo has announced that its language test is not available in Iran or for…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

Duolingo has announced that its language test is not available in Iran or for holders of Iranian identity documents. At the same time, reports have emerged of TOEFL test cancellations and no new dates being announced for the exam in Iran. These developments come a few days after the suspension of one of the US sanctions waivers related to educational services for Iranians. On August 24, the US Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) suspended for an indefinite period the general license known as "G," which since 2014 had permitted certain academic exchanges and the provision of educational services to Iranians. Duolingo, the American company behind the language-learning app whose online English test is accepted by many universities, has now stated on its official support page that the test is not available in Iran or for individuals using Iranian identity documents. Meanwhile, a number of Iranian users on social media have shared images that they say show TOEFL test cancellation messages and the absence of test centers or dates in the ETS registration system (the organizer of the TOEFL exam). Radio Farda cannot independently verify the authenticity or origin of these images. Some candidates have also said that TOEFL tests were being held in Iran until recently, but after OFAC's new decision, cancellation messages were sent to some applicants. As of the time of this report, the institution that administers the TOEFL exam had not issued an official statement about halting the test in Iran. On the institution's website, Iran still appears on the list of countries where the TOEFL iBT test is offered, and contact information specifically for Iranian applicants is also visible. Therefore, it remains unclear what scope the reported restrictions have and whether they are directly caused by OFAC's decision. The general license G, issued by OFAC in March 2014, among other things allowed accredited American universities to have academic exchange programs with Iranian universities and to provide certain educational services to Iranian students.@VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Order to silence! The last time I told someone it would be better to stay…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Order to silence! The last time I told someone it would be better to stay silent instead of speaking was in the middle of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad's first presidential term, addressing the late Seyed Ebrahim Nabavi. Of course, I didn't want him to be silent, but rather advised him to focus on satire and not get into serious political issues! Then I thought to myself, where does all this sense of wisdom, or really, my arrogance, come from? Why should I have the right to comment on political issues but Nabavi shouldn't? If he had turned around and told me: Why are you meddling in satirists' affairs for no reason? Sit down and write your serious stuff, how would I have felt? We have the right to criticize and reject others' opinions and ask them to be more careful, studied, and considerate in their expression, but where does the order to silence those whose views we don't like or don't find sound, for whatever reason, come from? I actually wrote this memory and its follow-up in support of the right to free speech of Mohammad Jafar Qaempanah, the vice president. Mr. Qaempanah has expressed an opinion about the importance and value of uranium enrichment in the country that some don't like, but instead of logical criticism, they call on him to be silent! Many also consider these people's own views to be wrong—would they like it if they were ordered to be silent by them? #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

The revolutionary current! Who exactly are the "revolutionary current" in the country, whose feelings and interests most officials are concerned about? Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of Parliament, has repeatedly emphasized that the hard core of power in the Islamic Republic is all 90 million Iranian citizens, but when it comes to responding to Hossein Shariatmadari's criticism, he introduces him as one of the "commanders of soft war" and "among the vanguard defenders of the Islamic Revolution"! The more I scrutinize the language of the media and official authorities, the more I conclude that, in their view, the "revolutionary current" refers to none other than those who share Mr. Shariatmadari's views and the supporters of the Front of Steadfastness! Well, what is the relationship of this current with the general public? If it is merely a subset of the people and has equal rights like other citizens, then on what basis are their sensitivities and interests preferred over other segments? And if it is opposed to the rest of the people, then what is that 90-million hard core of power that is being touted? That is, according to that sarcastic poem by Vahshi Bafqi, is it to be from the courtyard to the rooftop for the "revolutionary current," and from the rooftop to the Pleiades for the rest of the people? #احمد_زیدآبادی@ahmadzeidabad

The Path of Return
Iranians abroad who see things differently from what is commonly called the "opposition" come under psychological and media pressure. Artists, in particular, are more exposed to such pressures and negative propaganda. Eventually, a time comes when they prefer returning to their homeland, despite all its problems, over enduring those conditions, and they set their sights on going back to their birthplace. With such a decision, the political atmosphere abroad intensifies against them, and they become the target of the darkest accusations. In fact, part of the opposition seeking the overthrow of the Islamic Republic, on the one hand, treats Iranian artists abroad with utter cruelty and intolerance at the slightest divergence from their own views, and on the other hand, blocks their path back to the homeland and out of that toxic environment with endless insults! Apparently, their goal is for these artists to remain in that foreign land and die of grief! Any artist or any intellectual who does not succumb to this atmosphere and chooses the path of return to their country should be congratulated and welcomed. Living in one's homeland is the natural and God-given right of every Iranian and has nothing to do with the government. Those who deny this right or tarnish its exercise are both cut from the same cloth, standing at the two extremes of the axis of villainy! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [sahandiranmehr] ✔️Returning to the homeland and fear of a rift in the opposition!…
entry.summary:
Source: @sahandiranmehr

✔️Returning to the homeland and fear of a rift in the opposition! ✍🏻Sahand Iranmehr
The return of an Iranian who has not taken up arms against his country, has not called for violence, and has not supported foreign aggression against Iran should, in principle, be a matter of course—not a political concession. If even a modicum of rationality were applied, thousands of compatriots at home who harbor the unavoidable dream of emigration could also stay put.
That the trouble-free return of a handful of compatriots today comes as a surprise to some is the result of conditions that have driven a wedge between the Iranian and his homeland—a wedge that has provided the perfect ecosystem for all kinds of crises to take root and, consequently, for those who profit from them to thrive. So if this fledgling and "still trembling sapling of return" is displeasing to some, it may be because they would rather not see even a single knot in this tangled skein of "Iran's situation" come undone. It is these knots, piled one upon another, that absolve reason from effort, keep the cauldron of rage simmering on its own, and turn blood into a commodity for trade and for garnering support among this lot.
If the fly flees the dunghill, these too abhor conflict and prefer union over separation; because in their view, if a knot is to be untied, it must first receive the blessing of a Homa's shadow, and portraits must dance upon the shoulders of rage and destruction, and a brother must hide a blade in his sleeve aimed at the jugular of his own kin; for in a politics built on elimination, reconciliation and return are sometimes more dangerous than defeat itself, and they stoke the fires of crisis more than ever.
In short, don't be too surprised if they say: "These permissions are meant to create a rift in the opposition!" And don't be astonished if, one distant day, when the Homa's shadow falls upon the nation and the bitter times have passed, this lost lot mourns the dissipation of the opposition and beats their heads in despair!
These returns are, of course, good; even better is when all these differences and even hair-pulling squabbles take place within Iran, under the red line of "Iran." But sit back and watch how, in the days ahead, the knife and cheese—both inside and outside, with seemingly opposing edges—will secretly join hands to stitch the earth to the sky for this trembling, fledgling endeavor. Freeing Iran from its troubles has long since, for some, ceased to be a struggle for change and become a furnace to fan the flames within; and that is how, instead of thinking about solving its problems, they think about keeping them unsolved—and we've seen that if they catch wind of a "Truman Plus" that could wrap things up, they'll cheer for that too.
@sahandiranmehr

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic, in response to the new round of US economic pressure, has called on countries around the world to refrain from implementing Washington's unilateral sanctions against Iran. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic also criticized the United Nations and its member states for what it called "complacency" in the face of US and Israeli actions. This position was taken after the United States announced on Monday, August 23, the launch of a new campaign called "Operation Economic Outcast" against the Islamic Republic. The stated goal of this campaign is to intensify pressure on Iran's economic relations with other countries through threats of secondary sanctions and restrictions on access to the US financial system. entry.title: [bijanabdolkarimi] Civilizational Iranian-Islamic Intellectualism ✍️ Seyyed Mohammad Javad…
entry.summary:
Source: @bijanabdolkarimi

Civilizational Iranian-Islamic Intellectualism ✍️ Seyyed Mohammad Javad Bani Saeed Langeroudi. Intellectualism in Iran after the Islamic Revolution is not merely faced with the issue of critiquing tradition or adapting and localizing new theories; rather, the more fundamental issue is the possibility of the formation of "Iranian-Islamic civilizational intellectualism": an intellectualism that can create a coherent, rational, and path-opening system in the relationship between truth and reality, revelation and reason, identity and progress, heritage and future, and historical belonging and social responsibility. This article, with a conceptual, normative, and civilizational approach, addresses the formulation of the model of the civilizational intellectual. Its main claim is that this model is neither limited to imitating dominant global concepts and theoretical frameworks, nor is it reduced to an uncritical defense of the past and tradition, nor does it see its function as justifying the status quo; rather, it is an epistemic, moral, and social activism that, relying on revelatory sources, demonstrative rationality, the historical experience of Iran and Islam, and a precise understanding of contemporary issues and developments, seeks to produce concepts, theorize, and open the civilizational horizon of society. Civilizational intellectualism is truth-oriented and independent in knowledge; it understands religion as a system with explanatory capacity and social orientation; it reconciles critique and defense, loyalty and reform, and idealism and realism; and it regards critique not merely as negation and denial, but as a prelude to establishment, offering alternatives, and institution-building. Epistemic independence, conscious historical belonging, conceptual production, problem-orientation, foundational critique, responsible presence in the public sphere, the ability to combine rationality and spirituality, and attention to education and institution-building are among the fundamental components of this model. At the end, the article examines the epistemic, educational, and institutional requirements for the realization of such intellectualism. 🔗 Read the full note @bijanabdolkarimi

entry.title: [VahidOnline] The Trump administration has told mediators that it has no desire to return to…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

The Trump administration has told mediators that it has no desire to return to the terms of the initial June agreement with the Islamic Republic. This stance has hindered the renewed efforts of Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan to revive talks between Washington and Tehran. The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday, citing informed sources, that the Trump administration has repeatedly conveyed this position to mediators. The initial agreement, brokered by Pakistan, sought the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the start of talks on the Islamic Republic's nuclear program, and an end to the war. In return, sanctions relief and Tehran's access to frozen assets were envisioned. According to the Wall Street Journal, Trump has now prioritized economic pressure on the Islamic Republic and is prepared to wait to see the outcome of this policy. Anna Kelly, a White House spokesperson, also said no negotiations with the Islamic Republic are underway or planned, and the naval blockade and "economic exclusion operation" will continue. This report was published as Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir, traveled to Tehran earlier this week for talks. Oman's foreign minister has also held discussions with Islamic Republic officials to reach an understanding on the shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar's prime minister also met with Islamic Republic officials in Tehran on Thursday. The Wall Street Journal wrote that the dispute over how to interpret the June agreement and the conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz has made it difficult to reach a framework for resuming talks. Meanwhile, Tehran insists on implementing the terms of the previous agreement, while Washington pursues a path of economic pressure. @VahidOOnLine📡 @VahidOnline

entry.title: [sahandiranmehr] ✔️Ali Karimi and Three Thought-Provoking Frames ✍🏻Sahand Iranmehr…
entry.summary:
Source: @sahandiranmehr

✔️Ali Karimi and Three Thought-Provoking Frames ✍🏻Sahand Iranmehr
Frame One: Ali Karimi began his so-called political career with insults, and now the very same people who cheered him on are busy insulting him.
Frame Two: A few days ago, I was watching a video of some of those residing in America who call themselves the "Immortal Guard," engaged in so-called military drills in the woods, flaunting their weapons and mocking those who talk about reading books and awareness.
Frame Three: Not long ago, one of these individuals, referring to my novels, commented on a piece I had written: "Go write your novel."
Final Word: In my first novel, "Report of the Last Summer," I wrote through the voice of a character who was once a guerrilla and, decades later, looks back at those memories with a cautionary eye: "We thought we could leave the violence we wielded in the streets at the doorstep and live differently at home." Today's saga of Ali Karimi is one manifestation of a situation that is hardly strange or unpredictable for someone who has read a few books and novels instead of flaunting a weapon or the sharpness of juicy insults. Sometimes, to escape the violence done to oneself, one transfers that very violence to another. To escape humiliation, one humiliates. To avoid being a victim, one creates victims. To avoid being under someone's thumb, one raises one's own hand against another—and when one becomes the initiator of this path, one becomes its victim. Seeing these people and their experiences shows that knowing, reading, and understanding this futile method is no longer a decorative virtue; it is a way to avoid falling into this cycle and not to be surprised when the equation is inverted.
@sahandiranmehr

entry.title: [VahidOnline] Asieh Ramezani, a 39-year-old woman and mother of two, was killed by direct…
entry.summary:
Source: @VahidOnline

Asieh Ramezani, a 39-year-old woman and mother of two, was killed by direct fire from Islamic Republic forces during the suppression of the December 2025 protests in Tehran. Agents shot Ramezani from behind at close range in the early morning of Friday, January 9, 2026. The bullet passed through her back and chest, reaching her heart and killing her. Asieh Ramezani was the mother of a teenage daughter and an elementary school-aged son. Her family says that after the shooting, she was taken to a clinic but was left bleeding for about five hours without effective medical treatment. After losing track of her fate, Ramezani's family spent three days searching for her between the Kahrizak forensic medicine center and Behesht-e Zahra cemetery until they finally found her body. When the family found Ramezani's body, her cheek was bruised, and blood was still visible from under the cover in which the body had been placed. They said her body had been kept in "unworthy and painful" conditions. Ramezani's family also says her clothes, shoes, and other personal belongings were removed and not returned to them. After receiving the body, they realized that Ramezani's heart, which had been torn open by the bullet, had been stitched up without their knowledge. In their account, Asieh Ramezani's family wrote: "We will not forget those three days. We will not forget those five hours, that blood, that cover, that torn heart, and the belongings that should have been returned to her family." They emphasized that not all the facts surrounding her killing have yet been clarified, adding: "Even if a thousand years pass, the blood of our loved ones will not be washed away. We will repeat their names, keep their stories alive, and remain seekers of justice." @VahidHeadline📡 @VahidOnline

The prize was awarded to him at the official ceremony of World Water Week in Stockholm in recognition of his research and activities in water resource management, water governance, and providing innovative perspectives for addressing the water crisis. entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Dear Dr. Gerami, with greetings and respect. I hope you are well and healthy. I am a final-semester engineering student, about to enter the humanities at the master's level. For some time now, a question has been forming in my mind, the answer to which I have not found in texts, lectures, or lessons; for it is not a question of "what to read" or "how to write," but of "how to be." My concern is not the research method, but the researcher's character. More precisely, I want to know what qualities a humanities graduate must cultivate in themselves so that on the last day they are not merely a book-learned specialist, but a human being living in the deep and precise sense of the word. Does academic life, combined with pain and concern, require a "special character"? What kind of being is being a humanities student? Can this being be acquired through practice? Or is the answer fundamentally personal, and each person's path is unique to them? If possible, please guide me on this path from your perspective and lived experience. With infinite gratitude for the time you spend and renewed respect. 👇👇👇

entry.title: [bijanabdolkarimi] The Crisis of Self-Defeating and Short-Sighted Intellectualism ✍️ Seyyed…
entry.summary:
Source: @bijanabdolkarimi

The Crisis of Self-Defeating and Short-Sighted Intellectualism ✍️ Seyyed Mohammad Javad Bani Saeed Langeroudi

Decades after the victory of Iran's Islamic Revolution, one of the fundamental questions in the realm of social and cultural thought is: what relationship have intellectual elites and so-called intellectual currents established with the reconstruction of the national and religious identity of Iranian society? The historical expectation of the Iranian Muslim intellectual was that, in the face of the extensive epistemological, media, civilizational, and lifestyle onslaught of opposing currents, they would creatively revisit the heritage of Iran, Islam, and Islamic-Iranian civilization, and provide a new apparatus for its defense, explanation, and extension. However, in a significant portion of this current, instead of such a mission, one observes a kind of theoretical passivity, infatuation with modernity and postmodernity, distrust of indigenous heritage, and even alignment with aggressive discourses. This article, with a critical approach, examines the identity crisis of dependent intellectualism, its inability to formulate a new Iranian-Islamic identity, and the cultural, legal, economic, and social consequences of this inefficiency.

entry.title: [sahandiranmehr] 🔸️Ahmad asked: Are you back to writing again? At this age, with all these…
entry.summary:
Source: @sahandiranmehr

🔸️Ahmad asked: Are you back to writing again? At this age, with all these ailments, severe weakness, and failing eyesight, why do you shorten your life? Everything you have said and written so far, if read and heard, would suffice to awaken every sleeper and alert every conscious mind—yet you see that in the heart of the Iranian, it has had no more effect than raindrops on solid rock. And instead of acceptance and acknowledgment, you hear accusations of madness and weak faith? This is itself a wrong you do to yourself and your family.
🔸️A few days ago, in a gathering, your book was passed from hand to hand; one praised its binding, another described its calligraphy, a third admired its maps. One of the influential figures, clearing his throat in the inherited manner of our dear, undeserving leaders, said: I've heard the author of these reasonable absurdities is well-off and has means, but they say he's deranged. Whatever he says and writes is about reforming the homeland's flaws. Isn't there anyone to ask him: Good man, what has happened to our homeland, with its heavenly fruits and the aroma of bread found nowhere else, that it needs reforming?
🔸️Someone from the sidelines said: I've met him; you can't call him deranged. The poor fellow is unwell and suffers from severe self-importance. He approves of no one and no class in Iran. When I spoke of the "center," he said it is lawless and disorderly. When I asked about the governors, he said they are tyrants, oppressors, and bribe-takers. When I brought up the scribes, he said they draw the loops of "mim" and "noon" beautifully but know no geometry and have not studied arithmetic—may the devil take their calculations. When I asked about the seminary students, he said they know Yaghma the lyric poet well. When I inquired about the clerics, he said those in the holy shrines are free of greed, need no luxuries, and are content with cheese and onions instead of undue partridge and francolin stews—they are our spiritual fathers and, as successors to the Imams, must be obeyed. But most of those in Iran are hoarders and monopolists; they love chaos, relish the rabble's uproar, and worship the sound of clogs. They have annual incomes of thirty to fifty thousand tomans from their estates... When I asked about the merchants, he said they are frauds; apart from promoting the sale of foreign goods or hoarding grains, this class brings no benefit to the land or the nation...
🔸️After relaying this news, Ahmad sighed and said: "These words of mine suffice for you to consider all your efforts for this ignorant nation as blown to the wind, washed away by water, and burned by fire"...
🔸️I listened and became more despondent than Ahmad himself, wondering why he lets others' opinions dictate whether he acts or refrains.
✔️Masael al-Hayat
Mirza Abdolrahim Talibov Tabrizi
Constitutionalist Intellectual
@sahandiranmehr

Dear Dr. [Name], with greetings and respect. I hope you are well and in good spirits. I am a final-semester engineering student, on the verge of entering the humanities at the master's level. Or is the answer fundamentally personal, and each person's path unique to themselves? If possible, I would be grateful if you could guide me on this path from your own perspective and lived experience. With infinite thanks for the time you devote, and renewed respect.

Which massive base? The managing director of Kayhan newspaper, in his paper's "Note" column, addressed to Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of Parliament, wrote: "Some existing evidence suggests that a Western-oriented current and a number of reformist claimants have targeted changing Mr. Ghalibaf's 'social base' and are pursuing the transfer of his social base from among the vast and devoted masses of the people to the arena of political activity of reformist claimants and Western-oriented figures." Aside from what social base Mr. Ghalibaf has, what role he now seeks to play in the country's political developments, and what capabilities and limitations he faces, it is clear that the managing director of Kayhan, in his usual manner, is throwing dust in the eyes of the Speaker of Parliament to darken his view of the stark social realities in the country. The clearest evidence for this claim is the phrase "vast and devoted masses of the people" describing the social base of the faction affiliated with the managing director of Kayhan, which, in his view, Mr. Ghalibaf is supposedly going to leave behind to shift to the "arena of political activity of reformists"! Really, which "vast mass" in this country supports the faction affiliated with Hossein Shariatmadari and counts as its social base, that he warns Mr. Ghalibaf about losing this "vast popular base"? Iranian society and its diversity are before the eyes of every one of us, and any unbiased and healthy-minded person, by taking a look around this society, can discern the true size of the base of the force favored by Mr. Shariatmadari! Given this, why does the managing director of Kayhan distort reality? Is it because, due to being disconnected from society, he does not see reality? Or does he fundamentally have no interest in seeing reality? Or is he not so unaware of reality, but sees his own interest in distorting and presenting it upside down? I usually assumed that the country's decision-makers are themselves aware of these issues and dismiss claims like those of Kayhan, but some of them apparently not only do not dismiss Kayhan's claims but have come to believe that whatever it writes is exactly reality! If this point were not at stake, I would not spend my time responding to the managing director's quibbles.
#Ahmad_Zeydabadi
@ahmadzeidabad

Source: @yaser_arab57

.✍ Toto-chan
The book "The Dream School" is the true story of Toto-chan, a little Japanese girl, during her elementary school years. A little girl who later became a global figure. Why did she become a global figure? Because her mother didn't tell her until twenty years later that she had been expelled from school in that very first grade; she only said she wanted to take her to another school that she would love more. And that is the miraculous skill that many of us parents lack. This very "not saying" of one sentence completely changed Toto-chan's future, and it is because of not saying this one sentence that today the book Toto-chan holds the title of the best-selling book in Japan's history and has been translated into dozens of languages worldwide.
I won't tell you more than this, so you can read and hear it yourself. I have read this book once and listened to its audio version twice, and while reading this book, I cried several times for the injustice that goes on in the name of upbringing, at home and at school, against the children of my homeland. So definitely read or listen to it, even if you don't have children; and send it to anyone who has children or works with children: to fathers and mothers, to trainers, to teachers, and to anyone active in the field of childhood, education, and upbringing. Today (November 10th) has been designated by the United Nations as "World Science Day for Peace and Development." I am introducing this book today to remind that science by itself does not lead to peace and development. Science only serves peace and development when it is placed in the hands of humans who are enriched within and overflowing from without. And this enrichment and overflowing happen at home and at school. Toto-chan's story is the story of how a child is enriched internally and overflows externally. Toto-chan, the child of our story, is now ninety years old and is a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador and an advisor to the World Wide Fund for Nature. entry.title:
[mostafamalekian] 🔴 Hate the mistake, not the mistaken ✍️ Mostafa Malekian
One of the…
entry.summary:
Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴 Hate the mistake, not the mistaken
✍️ Mostafa Malekian

One of the important points in ethics is distinguishing the mistake from the mistaken. You can hate a bad deed, fight against it, and even prevent it from continuing—without hating the human being who committed that mistake.

Why?

• Hating the mistaken targets the person; whereas love for the human being is a prerequisite for reform. If we consider the person our enemy, then reforming them will no longer be our main goal.

• It helps us see our own mistakes too. When we focus on "finding faults" instead of "finding fault-doers," we realize that we ourselves might commit the same mistakes under certain circumstances.

• Emotions do not override rationality. Hatred of a person can impair our judgment and cause us to seek merely punishment or elimination of the individual, rather than correcting a behavior.

• We do not rush to eliminate the mistaken. The goal is not to eliminate the person; it is to stop the mistake and provide the possibility of reform.

This perspective does not mean being passive in the face of mistakes or injustice. You can firmly fight against a wrong behavior, even stop the mistaken person, but your motivation should not be personal revenge or hatred.

Gandhi has a saying that well illustrates this distinction:
"I hate the wrong deed, but I love human beings and do not hate those who do wrong."

Perhaps it is more ethical to say:
Fight the mistake, not the person.

Because if our goal is to reform the world, we cannot exclude human beings from the circle of our love and compassion—even when we must stand against their mistakes.

➖ Excerpt from the lecture series on Applied Ethics - Part Two - On Love and Compassion
@mostafamalekian

entry.title:
[vahidkarimipour] A word to students
After the letter from 46 professors of Sharif University of…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

A word to students

After the letter from 46 professors of Sharif University of Technology titled "For Sharif" was sent—which was in fact these colleagues' response to the "Letter from the Mothers of Students Expelled from Sharif"—I and at least four other colleagues who, unfortunately, did not have the honor of writing that letter but had signed it, received numerous messages from some students. All of them, while maintaining a polite tone, asked: "What was your feeling as signatories of this letter when the attack on Minab school happened?" and "Why did these professors not issue a statement at that time and condemn it?" This text is a response to those students.

The attack on Minab school and the killing of innocent children is undoubtedly a war crime. I hope that after the war ends, it will be pursued through an official complaint filed by the government and that appropriate compensation will be granted to the victims' families, although receiving compensation will never bring those innocent children back to their families' arms nor cool that eternal grief.

Therefore, the right way to deal with such atrocities is to pursue them through governmental and international institutions, not to have them condemned by this or that group of citizens. If the professors' letter had merely condemned the expulsion of students, it would have been a useless act as well. Instead, this letter contains a specific demand from the university president to review these rulings in accordance with revised procedures.

And now a word to the students who are dissatisfied with this letter and still support the expulsion of a group of their classmates. In my opinion, in any country in the world, the human and moral duty of a citizen is to side with a fellow citizen when they are up against organizations and institutions, to listen to their words, and to demand fair treatment for them, rather than siding with that organization or institution. The reason is very simple: because even an organization like the municipality is powerful enough and, when facing a citizen, does not need the support of another citizen. Even if a student lives in the most democratic country in the world, when it comes to a student versus an organization, ethically one should stand by one's classmate, not by that organization. For a student, being on a committee where another student—their classmate—receives an expulsion ruling is never a commendable act, and perhaps years later, when the fervor of youth subsides, it will bring shame and regret.

entry.title: [vahidkarimipour] The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at…
entry.summary:
Source: @vahidkarimipour

The following letter has been written by a group of mothers of students at Sharif University of Technology to one of our colleagues, and in fact to the entire body of colleagues at Sharif University of Technology. Its audience is, in reality, all professors and officials of Iranian universities.——————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————————-We are a group of mothers whose children have, in recent months, faced heavy disciplinary rulings and expulsion from university. We write this letter not out of confrontation, nor to disregard the rules, but from the position of mothers who are worried about the future, the fate, and the lost years of youth of their children, and we have turned to you with great hope. Our children may have made mistakes or committed violations under certain circumstances, and it is natural that the university has the right to react to violations; but is taking away the opportunity to continue education and destroying the future path of a young person the only possible response to a mistake? What pains us most of all is the severity and sometimes irreparability of the punishment that affects the future of these young people. Many of these students have strived for years to get into Sharif University, have completed a significant portion of their studies, and their families have placed all their hope and resources into their future. What is most painful for us is that some of these students, in addition to the disciplinary case at the university and the expulsion ruling, have also faced punishment from the judicial system (mostly one to three years of imprisonment); that is, for a single offense at the university, they have faced two punishments from two institutions—the university and the judicial system! We ask you, if possible, to hear the voice of these mothers and, to the extent of your ability, help in reviewing the expulsion rulings, converting heavy punishments into more proportionate rulings, and providing the possibility for these students to return to the path of education. Sometimes a second chance can save a young person's life. We do not expect you to disregard the law; we only ask that alongside the law, fairness, proportionality of punishment, the circumstances of each student, and the future of a human being also be considered. If you have the means to follow up on these concerns or convey them to university officials or officials of the Ministry of Science, we sincerely request that you do not leave us alone. We thank you in advance for the time you take to hear our voice. With respect and hope, a group of mothers of expelled students of Sharif University of Technology

No information has been published about Adineh's access to a lawyer of his choice, the judicial process, the timing of the trial, or how his statements were obtained. The execution of Majid Adineh follows the ongoing implementation of death sentences against detainees from the Dey protests. On Mordad 21, 1405 (August 12, 2026), more than 30 countries issued a joint statement condemning the continued issuance and execution of death sentences against Iranian protesters as a tool to "silence the voices of opponents." entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Did anyone say...? Pejman Jamshidi's sister has said; my brother is not an…

Did anyone say...? Pejman Jamshidi's sister has said; my brother is not an Imamzadeh! Did anyone say he was an Imamzadeh? In 1996, I interviewed Mohammad Javad Larijani when he was the head of the Parliament Research Center and a disciple of Sheikh Ali Akbar Nategh Nouri, in a building in Baharestan Square. The interview was supposed to be published in Hamshahri newspaper, but the newspaper's officials found it too challenging and set it aside. In that interview, I strongly challenged Mr. Larijani on the degree of democracy in the Islamic Republic system using the criterion that Karl Popper provides, and I put him in a tight spot! He spoke a eloquent chapter in denunciation of Popper, which I answered; to hell with Popper! You tell me, according to the criterion he proposed, how democratic is the Islamic Republic? In short, to accept a low level of my criticisms, he was forced to say; the members of the Guardian Council are not infallible! I said; did anyone even entertain the suspicion of their infallibility? I should not forget to mention that the transcribed text of that interview sat in the drawer of the newspaper office's desk for a long time until Saeed Laylaz became the head of a newly established section in Hamshahri called the interview section. One night when he was left empty-handed to fill the page and was searching desperately for content, I remembered the interview with Mr. Larijani and suggested publishing it to Mr. Laylaz! Happy and smiling, he took the interview text and printed it in Hamshahri over two issues, but the challenging and valuable parts of the interview were completely removed from the published text. Regarding Pejman Jamshidi's verdict, I also did not understand the case! Apparently, the court acquitted him of the rape charge and sentenced him to flogging for an act contrary to Sharia! If there was no rape, then what other act is contrary to Sharia? Has the judge issuing the verdict not heard the recent remarks of Hassan Rahimpour Azghadi? He has explicitly said that with mutual consent, even two schoolchildren before puberty can have sexual relations and this act has no religious flaw or problem. According to Mr. Azghadi's calculation, if in the case of Mr. Jamshidi's accusation there was mutual consent, then where in the story is it contrary to Sharia that makes his flogging necessary? And if one side did not consent, then how was the acquittal of the rape charge established? #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

entry.title: [hesmashena] The real innovation of this plan lies in five points: The policy unit shifts…
entry.summary:
Source: @hesmashena

The real innovation of this plan lies in five points: The policy unit shifts from "carrier" to "service." Today, gasoline, gas, electricity, water, and transportation are largely managed in separate platforms. The plan says every decision should be measured based on the final output: "one unit of cooling," "one unit of heating," and "one unit of mobility" — with what combination of resources, technology, and cost they are provided. Four sources and three services are placed in a common decision matrix. For example, replacing gasoline with electricity is only desirable if its effect on the electricity balance, power plant gas, air, and network cost is measured simultaneously. This prevents "transferring imbalance from one carrier to another." Price reform becomes a functional contract rather than a financial measure. The price of excess consumption only rises when a real possibility of reducing consumption has been created; in mobility, that means travel options; in heating, controls and equipment; in cooling, low-consumption technology. This is an operational rule, not a slogan. Instead of buying equipment, the government buys "verified savings." Heaters, coolers, motors, buses, or boiler rooms are not the main subjects of payment. Payment is made against cubic meters of gas, kilowatt-hours of electricity, cubic meters of water, peak megawatts, or actually freed fuel. This change alters the financial and incentive model of the program. Three major consumption markets are redesigned simultaneously and complementarily. In mobility: vehicle–energy–time–cost; in heating: building–equipment–control–behavior; in cooling: electricity–water–peak–comfort. Thus, instead of dozens of scattered projects, three national "savings factories" are formed.

entry.title: [hesmashena] This separation prevents the organization from getting bogged down in…
entry.summary:
Source: @hesmashena

This separation prevents the organization from getting bogged down in implementation details and losing its main mission, which is increasing the overall system's productivity. The ultimate success criterion: The program's success should not be measured by the number of heaters, coolers, buses, or motorcycles replaced. The right measure is the amount of service produced with fewer resources. In cooling: reduced electricity, water, and peak demand against maintained comfort. In heating: reduced gas and winter peak against maintained comfort. In mobility: energy consumed per passenger-kilometer or ton-kilometer. At the macro level, the final indicator is: providing more or better cooling, heating, and mobility with less water consumption, less damage to air and soil, less energy, and lower public cost. This framework can transform the organization's 24-month program from a set of scattered projects into a coherent and measurable policy. In this view, gasoline, gas, electricity, coolers, heaters, boiler rooms, and vehicles are not themselves the "problem"; they are tools for providing three main services with higher efficiency and less pressure on the country's four basic resources.

entry.title: [jalaeipour] Education and health in the employment structure In the European Union, the…
entry.summary:
Source: @jalaeipour

Education and health in the employment structure
In the European Union, the share of education and health in total employment is about 22 percent. In some Northern European countries, this ratio reaches 30 percent. More than 70 percent of jobs in these two sectors are held by women (approximately one-third of total female employment is in these two sectors).
In Turkey, Malaysia, Japan, South Korea, Algeria, and Tunisia, the share of these two sectors in total employment is about 11 percent, and in South America it averages between 11 and 12 percent.
The share of education and health in employment in Iran, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Bangladesh is about 8 percent. Apart from the role that education and health play in societal self-reliance, individual autonomy, citizenship, and social reproduction, even from an economic perspective, investment in these two sectors is highly effective in economic reproduction and growth. In Iran, input-output tables confirm this impact. Nevertheless, these two sectors in Iran face serious shortages in terms of financing, human resources, and infrastructure. This issue is particularly important given Iran's population dispersion and area. In this regard, this comparison might be interesting: the number of students in Iran is almost twice that of England, and the number of schools in Iran is more than four times. Iran's area is also about 12 times that of England. In Iran, more than 30 percent of students study in private and semi-private schools, while in England it is about 6 percent. However, the teaching staff of the two countries is almost equal.
In Iran, since the late 1980s, these two sectors have been the focus of government downsizing. Layers of the middle and upper classes also went along with these policies. But beyond the issue of government downsizing, the two institutions that are essential both for societal reproduction and economic growth were seen as surplus costs. According to one of the ministers of the first Hashemi government, some economists justified that these two sectors had the largest share of the government budget, and if only a little of these two were handed over to the private sector, the government's budget deficit would reach zero. He says we were "deceived" and accepted, but the more we handed over from these two sectors, the larger the budget deficit became.
Postscript: Education and health are two main areas of social investment, and there is great emphasis on investing in these two areas to face new risks. In successful experiences, due to the related and intertwined issues of these two areas, extensive job clusters have been formed at national and local levels.
@Omidi_Reza

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Defective Structure of Consciousness! Why is there so much emphasis in Persian…
entry.summary:
Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Defective Structure of Consciousness! Why is there so much emphasis in Persian literature on learning lessons from history? For the obvious reason that we Iranians have the least interest in learning lessons from history; otherwise, why would this topic be repeated to such an extent? The experience of August 28, 1953 (28 Mordad 1332) is right before our eyes! No political force can be found that has learned the necessary lesson from that event. The descendants of all the forces that played a role, negatively or positively, in that catastrophe are not only repeating those mistakes but have intensified their errors. Is it, as Ahmad Shamlou said, that our historical memory as Iranians is weak? The weakness of historical memory is not without a role in this matter, but in my opinion, the "defective structure of consciousness" plays a much larger role. The structure of consciousness in any society, in my view, is much more important than other structures, and until it is reformed, the reform of political and social structures seems impossible. Political and social structures can be shattered by revolt and revolution, but if the structure of consciousness is not sound, those two structures will be reproduced in a more horrific way. Reforming the structure of consciousness of a society, however, is infinitely difficult, because first, reaching a collective agreement on the criteria for whether a thought or consciousness is defective or sound, especially in a society where everyone is infatuated with their own thoughts, is beyond difficulty. Second, the prerequisite for reforming the structure of society's consciousness begins with self-criticism and continues with the necessary patience to convince others through discussion and dialogue. In our country, self-criticism is considered a sign of weakness and is truly seen as self-flagellation. Hence, finding faults must be sought not in one's own camp but in the opposing camp. When we do not acknowledge any weakness for ourselves and see our own camp at the "tip of the arrow of historical evolution!" it is natural that we also do not find the patience for persuasive dialogue and consider the elimination, disregard, and belittlement of others as an easier path! In short, for historical reasons, we have developed a defective structure of consciousness, and again for historical reasons, we have shown and do not show any interest in reforming it. Hence, we repeat our fate in a closed circle. This time, however, the previously traveled paths are also blocked. Therefore, the most astonishing events in history await us. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad
